t: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Federal building and United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “R.E. Thomason Federal Building and United States Courthouse”.

fable.w: This is a boilerplate naming provision stating how references to a federal building in federal records are to be read. The word "regulation" might tempt a Yes reading, but it appears only in a list of existing records and does not authorize or require rulemaking. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be deemed to be a reference to the “R.E. Thomason Federal Building and United States Courthouse”

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely administrative renaming provision. It dictates how a specific federal building should be referred to in official records. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government, nor does it establish any advisory bodies or public comment periods.
qwen_block.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the Federal building and United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “R.E. Thomason Federal Building and United States Courthouse”.

No federal decision involves states, the public, experts or any other outside party. The word "regulation" just lists types of records and doesn't authorize rulemaking, so it isn't participation.
